title: corpus
description: A structured analysis of the reels you saved because you admired them. This is your taste, made machine-readable. It describes OTHER people's work - what you can learn from it - and never your own claims (those live in voice.json).

method.description: How this corpus was produced. Recorded so a later rebuild can be compared like-for-like.

sources.description: The creators you pulled from. Two or three contrasting creators beats one, because the contrast is what tells you which parts are style and which are structure.

why_saved.description: In your own words, what made you save these. Written before analysis, so the analysis cannot rationalize itself.

reels.description: One entry per analyzed reel. Fewer than about 10 and the aggregate numbers are noise rather than a pattern.

scene_count.description: Detected hard cuts or large compositional changes. Undercounts micro-motion, caption changes and progressive reveals - treat as a floor, not a total.

content_structure.description: The beat sequence, in order, in plain language. e.g. ['problem hook','named mechanism','three examples','contrarian turn','resource CTA']

lesson.description: The single transferable lesson. If you cannot state it without naming the creator's specific topic, you have described the skin rather than the grammar.

per_creator.description: Kept per-creator on purpose. Averaging two creators with different pacing into one house number destroys the thing that made each of them work.

engines.description: The repeatable content engine behind each creator, plus an honest note on what breaks if you copy it wholesale.

shared_grammar.description: What every analyzed reel does regardless of creator. These are the closest thing to laws in the corpus.

differences.description: Where the creators diverge, and which side you should take.

visual_modes.description: The small set of presentation modes the corpus actually uses. Videos feel varied because modes are sequenced differently, not because every sentence gets a new design.

mode_selection_rules.description: Spoken beat -> default mode. The lookup table that stops visual choice from being re-litigated on every line.

pacing_targets.description: Starting guardrails derived from the measured numbers above, not laws.

typography_hierarchy.description: The distinct text roles observed. Collapsing these into one caption component is a known failure mode.

motion_hierarchy.description: Ordered from most to least meaningful. Motion below the comprehension line is decoration.

anti_patterns.description: Things the corpus shows you should NOT do. Often more useful than the positive rules.

synthesis.description: The point of the whole exercise: not to imitate any one creator, but to name the combination you are actually going for.

explicitly_not.description: What you are deliberately leaving behind from this creator.

script_formula.description: Your default beat sequence, derived from the engines above. The script agent starts here and departs from it deliberately, not accidentally.
